survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: ICCS 2009 used a two-stage cluster sampling design: schools were sampled with probability proportional to size (PPS) and intact Grade 8 (or equivalent) classrooms were sampled within schools. The report describes calculating student, teacher, and school sampling weights to represent the defined target populations in each participating country, and it also documents participation-rate adjustments. For variance estimation, the jackknife repeated replication (JRR) method was used: schools were paired into sampling zones (pseudo-strata), and replicate weights were created by setting one PSU’s contribution to zero and doubling the paired PSU’s contribution within each zone. For civic knowledge test scores, standard errors also incorporate plausible-value imputation variance by using all five plausible values when estimating population statistics.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is an official IEA/OECD technical report or assessment framework. It describes sampling, scaling, and instrument design rather than student-level predictive modeling. Plausible values are therefore not applicable to the document's primary analytic purpose; any missing-data discussion refers to fieldwork or scaling procedures, not a single ML imputation strategy.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: ICCS 2009 targeted Grade 8 (or equivalent) students with an average age of at least 13.5 years at assessment time. The student sample was drawn as a two-stage cluster sample: schools were selected using PPS based on enrollment size, and within each sampled school an intact class from the target grade was randomly sampled and all students in that class were surveyed. The report also documents exclusions at the school level by country (e.g., special education schools, very small schools, and other coverage exclusions) and participation requirements at the within-school level (e.g., schools treated as non-participating when within-school participation rate was below 50%). For multivariate analyses, students with no student questionnaire data were excluded, and for remaining cases a dummy-variable adjustment was applied with mean/median substitution for missing predictor values.

data.outcome_summary: ICCS 2009 is a comparative international survey of civic and citizenship education administered to Grade 8 (or equivalent) students, complemented by teacher and school principal questionnaires and a national contexts survey. The cognitive test used Rasch-based item response modeling to derive civic knowledge scores from 79 (of 80) items, and the report uses plausible value methodology with five separate estimates per student for reporting civic knowledge. The final reporting scale was standardized to an international metric (mean 500, SD 100 for equally weighted national samples), with proficiency levels defined by scale-point cut-points. The survey employed two-stage cluster sampling (PPS school sampling and intact classroom sampling) across 38 countries, with sampling weights and jackknife repeated replication (JRR) used to estimate sampling variance. For multivariate analyses, missing data were handled via dummy-variable adjustment and mean/median substitution, and standard errors incorporated both sampling and imputation components for plausible-value-based outcomes.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This document is an IEA technical report describing ICCS 2009 instrument development, sampling, scaling, and reporting procedures rather than an empirical predictive/causal study with ML model training and reported target-specific performance. As a result, there are no distinct ML target variables with model metrics to extract, and the schema’s main_findings and confounders_identified are intentionally left empty. The report does, however, specify the psychometric scaling approach (Rasch, IRT/WLE, CFA for questionnaire scales) and the variance estimation framework (JRR and plausible-value imputation variance), which are methodological rather than ML-predictive results.
